BUG: LaneHibernator.resume() lets a failing reacquire hook propagate as an exception, leaving the lane HIBERNATED with a partially reacquired resource set and no failure report
CONFLICTING_OWNER: NONE (no active lane claims provider_hibernation.py; provider continuity shipped in PR #128)
MINIMAL_FIX: Mirror hibernate()'s failed[] accounting in resume(): catch per-hook exceptions, collect failed names into a resume report (returned, not raised), keep the lane in a defined state (e.g. stay HIBERNATED when anything failed, ACTIVE only when all reacquired), and only mark res.released=False after its hook succeeds. Pin with a test: failing reacquire hook -> report names the resource, lane stays HIBERNATED, failed resource still released=True.
RAW_EVIDENCE: scripts/provider_hibernation.py resume(): hook(name) result/exception unhandled; res.released=False runs only on success path, so a raise skips it for that resource AND aborts the loop for the rest; lane.state stays HIBERNATED; nothing records which resource failed (hibernate() by contrast builds failed[] + release_report and degrades to ACTIVE). Probe /tmp/probe_p2_hibernate.py prints PARTIAL_UNREPORTED=True. CODEX_PROVIDER_CONTINUITY.md requires 'Release failures remain visible' and idempotent hooks that verify identity; the resume half has neither.
REPRO_STEPS: 1. LaneHibernator with resource gpu/kind=provider whose reacquire_hook raises, plus watcher with no-op hook. 2. hibernate(checkpoint) -> HIBERNATED. 3. resume() raises RuntimeError; lane stays HIBERNATED; watcher marked released=False although its hook verified nothing; gpu still released=True; no report exists. See /tmp/probe_p2_hibernate.py.
TARGETED_TEST: Register a reacquire hook that raises, hibernate, call resume, and assert a failure report names the resource with the lane left HIBERNATED (no bare exception, no silent partial state).
